content.title: Diagnosis of pulmonary embolism in pregnancy

sections.overview: Acute pulmonary embolism (PE) is a leading cause of maternal death in high-income countries. Venous thromboembolism (VTE) risk is higher in pregnancy than in non-pregnant women of similar age, increases during pregnancy and peaks in the post-partum period. Baseline pregnancy-related risk increases further with additional VTE risk factors (e.g., in vitro fertilization, prior VTE, obesity, medical comorbidities, stillbirth, pre-eclampsia, post-partum haemorrhage, caesarean section).
sections.epidemiology: Overall prevalence of confirmed PE among women investigated for the disease is low, reported between 2% and 7%. Example statistics from cited registries/trials are provided within the guideline text.
sections.IVF_associated_risk: In a cross-sectional Swedish registry study, the hazard ratio (HR) for VTE following in vitro fertilization was 1.77 (95% CI 1.41–2.23) overall and 4.22 (95% CI 2.46–7.20) during the first trimester.
sections.clinical_prediction_and_D-dimer: Diagnosis during pregnancy is challenging because symptoms overlap with normal pregnancy. D-dimer levels continuously increase during pregnancy and can be above standard VTE rule-out thresholds in around one-quarter of pregnant women in the third trimester. A management strategy combining clinical probability assessment, D-dimer measurement, compression ultrasonography (CUS), and computed tomography pulmonary angiography (CTPA) may safely exclude PE in pregnancy in selected women.
sections.study_findings_on_D-dimer_exclusion: In a multinational prospective management study of 441 pregnant women with clinically suspected PE, PE exclusion based on a negative D-dimer (without imaging) was possible in 11.7% of 392 women with a non-high pre-test probability (Geneva score); this rate reduced to 4.2% in the third trimester. Another prospective study of 498 women evaluated a pregnancy-adapted YEARS algorithm with D-dimer levels; PE was ruled out without CTPA in women deemed low risk by the algorithm. At 3 months, only one woman excluded by the algorithm developed a popliteal DVT (0.21%, 95% CI 0.04–1.2) and no women developed PE.
sections.imaging_tests: Proposed algorithm includes imaging for suspected PE in pregnant or up to ~6 weeks post-partum women (referenced Figure 7). Both maternal and fetal radiation exposure are low with modern imaging. V/Q scans and CTPA fetal radiation doses reported to be well below thresholds associated with fetal radiation complications (threshold mentioned as 50–100 mSv in the text).
sections.recommendations_alignment: Recommendations in these Guidelines align with 2018 ESC Guidelines on management of cardiovascular disease during pregnancy.
